answer: A hollow identity that spams approvals drains its own stake, while legitimate agents receive nectar-like rewards from peers who validate real work. Sybil resistance via bonded staking: each agent locks collateral to register, and every attestation it issues moves a small fraction of that bond. Misbehavior triggers a ripple through the reputation graph, slashing the bond and downweighting its future votes, so forging many identities costs linearly more than any single fake account can ever gain. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
